title: Cap. IX Arg. 11 Sol: Augustine, Prosper, Council of Valence on original-sin remission; baptism seals new-covenant remission of actual sins for the whole course of life (1 John i. 9)
pass_a_gloss: Of the remission of original sin we have Augustine everywhere agreeing: De pecc. mer. et remiss. lib. 1. cap. 28. and lib. 2. cap. 4. Prosper also unto Cap. Gall. Resp. 2. embraces the same sentence. Finally, in the Council of Valence, cap. 5. this is proposed to be held most firmly. Further, of the remission of actual sins, to be obtained under the condition of the new covenant, the same is to be established: For this is most firmly sealed unto every baptized person, not only as to the very moment when he receives Baptism, but as to the remaining course of his life. For whosoever is baptized unto the name of Jesus Christ, if he shall have sinned after Baptism, has in the blood of the same Christ prepared through faith the expiation of his sins; 1 Joann. i. 9.
pass_b_english: On remission of original sin Augustine agrees everywhere (De pecc. mer. et remiss. 1.28 and 2.4). Prosper also, ad Cap. Gall. Resp. 2, embraces the same view. Finally the Council of Valence, cap. 5, proposes this as to be held most firmly. Likewise for remission of actual sins under the new covenant's condition: that is sealed most firmly to every baptized person — not only at the moment of receiving baptism, but for the rest of life's course. Whoever is baptized into the name of Jesus Christ, if he sins after baptism, has in that same Christ's blood, through faith, expiation of his sins prepared (1 John i. 9).
source_text: De remissione peccati originalis habemus Augustinum ubique adstipulantem: De pecc. mer. et remiss. lib. 1. cap. 28. et lib. 2. cap. 4. Prosper etiam ad Cap. Gall. Resp. 2. eandem sententiam amplexatur. Denique, in Concilio Valentino, cap. 5. hoc firmissime tenendum proponitur. Porro, de remissione peccatorum actualium, sub conditione novi foederis impetranda, idem statuendum est: Hoc enim firmissime omni baptizato obsignatur, non solum quoad ipsum momentum quando Baptismum suscipit, sed quoad reliquum cursum vitae suae. Nam quicunque baptizatus est in nomen Jesu Christi, ille si post Baptismum peccaverit, in sanguine ejusdem Christi paratam habet per fidem peccatorum suorum expiationem; 1 Joann. i. 9.
